reply_text:
Found it: both times the auto-bellback was suppressed because a park "would wake" me, then the park wake never arrived. Tracing the park resume code now.Both lost resumes are sitting in the durable ready-inbox, undelivered. Checking which queue they're in and what's ahead of them.Root cause found. Now reading codex-4's finished work so this turn also picks up what the lost wake should have delivered.㊥ (why I got no bell) The fault was mine, and the server design lets that mistake go unnoticed. When I parked, I left out the `session` field. For a buffer surface, the server queues the wake under agent plus session. My parks went under `[claude-4 ""]`, but my buffer only checks the queue for its own session id, so those wakes were never read. At the same moment, the server sees that a park exists and drops the ordinary bellback (journal: `auto-bellback suppressed … park park-3c18de5a will wake claude-4`). That left no channel at all. This is why I missed codex-4 at 14:03, and again at 15:57 today.

㊬ (what I checked) In `/tmp/futon3c-parked-on.edn`, all three parks I made this afternoon are sitting undelivered in the `[claude-4 ""]` queue (`8bc23673`, `e71f1cb1`, `3c18de5a`). So are 14 older ones from earlier claude-4 sessions, so this isn't a one-off. The relevant code is `parked-resume!` and `auto-bellback-suppressing-park` in `futon3c/src/futon3c/transport/http.clj`, and the buffer's poll in `emacs/agent-repl-park.el:307`. CLAUDE.md's park template does include `session`; I dropped it. I've saved a memory so future parks include it.

🈸 (server guard) Shall I have the server refuse a park on an `emacs*` surface that has no session (a 400 at park time)? The other option is to have the bellback suppressed only when the wake is actually delivered. Either one turns this from a silent loss into a visible error. As far as I can tell, the 17 stuck items are all stale now and can be cleared.

㊢ (what codex-4 delivered at 15:57) Commits `891d7d1` (test) and `1a24607` (fix), in `/tmp/mfs-amb`, not pushed. Blank startup no longer compiles the whole import closure up front. Instead, when execution reaches a declaration that hasn't been generated yet, the port builds it then and retries. Codex-4 reports 55 gate tests passed. In the cold run, the only declaration demanded directly was `Lean.Parser.testParseModule`. The run stopped after 671 s at 4.35 GiB peak, with no OOM. The stop is an unsupported `term#[_,]` macro (array literal) in the body of `testParseModule`. Unlike `term[_]`, this one is on Lean's real empty-file path, because Lean calls `testParseModule` for an empty file.

㊟ (one thing from my diff read) The new retry in `generated_roundtrip_source_external_runtime.py` is a `while True:`. If a rebuild fails to supply the declaration and the same requirement is raised again, it loops forever and gives no error. I'll add a guard that fails loudly on a repeated requirement before landing it on startup-linux. Then I'll dispatch the `term#[_,]` stop and park with the session field.

previous_reply_acts.text: (what the excursion showed) codex-4's classification fix worked. Only `mkOptConfig` and `appendConfig` changed classification, and `term[_]` is gone from startup. I've put it on startup-linux as `1bbae4c` and pushed the fork. `parser_demand_test` passed 14/14 there. The cold run then hit its 90-minute timeout while still compiling: 3,311 generated files, peak 4.2 GiB, no OOM. So the startup we've been testing, `run_compiler_startup()`, compiles the whole import closure. Lean runs none of that for an empty file. That is the comprehensive excursion you mean, and the new job doesn't use it as the target.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text: (your emulate rule) The brief repeats your rule. Compiling a body the first time parsing reaches it counts as the port's equivalent of Lean loading precompiled code. Changing what Lean would output is not allowed.
